page: The Microsoft Azure DC16ads_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine designed for balanced compute and memory tasks. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it features a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V74 processor provisioned with 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores with two threads per core. Memory capacity is configured at 64.0 GB of RAM, establishing a standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The hardware profile includes a bundled 644 GB local SSD and supports Azure Premium Storage. It contains no GPU hardware and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, operating under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Instruction set features for the AMD EPYC processor include AVX, AES, VAES, SHA_NI, BMI2, and FMA, providing hardware-accelerated cryptographic processing. However, it lacks AVX-512 extensions and matrix acceleration extensions such as AMX. In standard compute benchmarks, the instance yields average tier results relative to comparable instances, scoring 2326.16 in stress-ng single-core and 18632.61 in multi-core testing. Geekbench results record a single-core score of 1222.0 and a multi-core score of 7333.0, alongside 12135.0 in Clang software compilation and 13880.0 in ray tracing tests. PassMark benchmarks show an overall CPU score of 19743.78, with an encryption sub-score of 13716.06 and a memory score of 2248.67.

Workload testing highlights throughput efficiency in data-centric operations, with Redis SET performance achieving 17.52 million operations per second and PassMark database operations scoring 6361.4. The bundled 644 GB local SSD provides fast scratch space, making the configuration effective for caching tiers, staging environments, relational databases, software build pipelines, and general enterprise application hosting. A primary architectural tradeoff is the absence of AVX-512 vector extensions and dedicated hardware accelerators, which constrains efficiency for intensive machine learning inference and high-performance computing tasks.

It provides 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores alongside 64.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. The configuration includes a bundled 644 GB local SSD and supports Premium Storage without dedicated GPU hardware. CPU instructions include hardware-accelerated AES, VAES, and AVX, while omitting AVX-512 support. Benchmark results demonstrate consistent middle-tier performance, logging 18632.61 in stress-ng multi-core, 7333.0 in Geekbench multi-core, and 17.52 million operations per second in Redis SET operations. With PassMark database scores reaching 6361.4, the instance delivers balanced compute density and integrated local storage suited for relational database operations, in-memory caching layers, enterprise application serving, and continuous integration workflows.
